title: CoreError type alias keeps two names alive for ValidationError with no migration path
description:
crates/core/src/error.rs line 280: pub type CoreError = ValidationError; with doc comment 'Backwards-compatibility alias. New code should use ValidationError directly.'

The alias is only used in article.rs (GroupName::new returns Result<_, CoreError>) and in error.rs's own test (test_core_error_alias_works). There is no external crate that depends on the CoreError name — all other crates import stoa_core directly and could use ValidationError. The 'backwards compatibility' comment implies a migration in progress, but there is no issue tracking the removal.

Fix: replace the two uses of CoreError in crates/core/ with ValidationError directly, then delete the alias. If there is a genuine external consumer that must not break, file an issue tracking it explicitly.
